To minimize adverse impacts during a water shortage condition, the City Council may be resolution or motion impose such restrictions on water use as are required to promote and protect the health, safety, and public welfare of the citizens of the City of Danielsville. The following water conservation stages and associated actions may be implemented by the City Council when deemed appropriate, as part of the drought continency plan for the City of Danielsville:

Stage | - Continuous Conservation - Improve water use habits, reduce wasting of water by increasing water use efficiency, and encourage the use of water devices to obtain a water consumption reduction goal of five percent (5%) by some or all of the following:

Encourage commercial and institutional water users to install recycle and conservation systems where feasible.

Stage II - Minor Conservation - All stage | actions will be continued and the following additional actions may be implemented to increase conservation to a goal of ten percent (10%) consumption reduction:

To: Permitted Water Providers

From: Carol A. Couch, Director, Georgia Environmental Protection Division Subject: Newly Adopted Rules for Outdoor Water Use

Date: June 4, 2004

The Board of Natural Resources adopted RULES FOR OUTDOOR WATER USE, Chapter 391-3- 30, at its regular meeting on May 26, 2004. Under the new rules, Georgians will be required to follow schedules for outdoor water use during both non-drought periods and during periods of declared drought. The rules are consistent with Section 4 (Drought Responses) of the Georgia Drought Management Plan, which the Board adopted last year.

The rules apply to any entity, and its customers, permitted by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) for water withdrawal or for the operation of a public drinking water supply system. There are some exemptions to these rules, including newly installed landscapes, golf courses and commercial uses. A copy of the rules is enclosed. The rules also are available at the EPD Web site www.dnr.state.ga.us/dnr/environ/ under the “Rules & Laws” section.

Local governments should begin enforcing the new watering schedules as soon as possible. We recognize that new ordinances may be required in some communities, and it will take time to enact those ordinances and educate citizens on the details of these new watering schedules. We will expect all providers to fully implement the Rules For Outdoor Water Use no later than August 1, 2004.

Current conditions warrant the non-drought schedule for outdoor water use statewide, but should conditions worsen, EPD will require that you immediately take action to manage outdoor water use appropriate to the level of declared drought in your area. Water providers are authorized to implement more stringent outdoor water use schedules within their jurisdictions.

Historically, Georgia's local governments and water providers have played a key role in getting citizens to comply with outdoor water use schedules. We would like to thank you for your help and ask for your continued support to protect and conserve our limited water resources. Cooperation from all Georgians is necessary for the implementation of these very important niles. We have included an outreach document on proper outdoor watering procedures, which can be shared with your customers. You also can visit www.conservewatergeorgia.net for more information.

Should you have any questions about the rules, please feel free to contact Jeff Lovegrove (404) 657- 7430, Tamara Frank (404) 651-6830 or John Otto (404) 651-8708 of the EPD Drinking Water Program, or Kevin Chambers, EPD Communications Director at (404) 656-4713.

The Georgia Drought Management Plan, effective March 26, 2003, calls for year-round outdoor water conservation practices whether we are in times of drought or not. On May 26, 2004, the Board of Natural Resources (DNR) adopted Rules for Outdoor Water Use (Chapter 391-3-30) that set a permanent outdoor water schedule in Georgia. Several local governments have decided to keep more restrictive schedules in place. We offer this brochure to explain why outdoor water conservation makes sense.

Reasons Why?

Water is a limited resource that needs to be used wisely. Outdoor water use can account for up to 50 % of total water use for a home during the summer months. Homes with automated irrigation systems are more likely to overuse outdoor water. Outdoor irrigation use can easily be reduced by applying water only when and where it is needed.

Over irrigation can damage plants or make plants unhealthy. In Georgia, the average rainfall is 54 inches a year. Often no supplemental watering is necessary to maintain a landscape. Supplemental irrigation is typically needed only when installing plants and in the summer on annuals that can dry up in the heat. Over-watered plants are more susceptible to disease and pest infestations.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are we implementing outdoor watering restrictions if there is no drought? In Georgia, the DNR is charged with managing water as a shared resource for the public good. Instituting outdoor water use policy during non-drought periods will make water conservation behavior a part of

Georgia culture and allow for reasonable water use during periods of drought.

Many times, enough outdoor water is provided by rain. During dry periods, watering deeply 3 days a week is sufficient to maintain a landscape. The University of Georgia College of Agriculture and Environmental Sciences drought web site states: "If citizens would learn about the water needs of plants and implement water-efficient landscape practices, outdoor water use could be decreased by 50 percent or more without sacrificing quality or beauty of the outdoor environment.”

See www.georgiadrought.org .

How do State regulations differ from local restrictions? Local restrictions can be the same as or stricter than State restrictions, but not less strict. It is important that you check with your local water utility provider to know what your local restrictions are.

391-3-30-.01 Definitions

When used in this Chapter: (1) “Address” means the “house number” (a numeric or alphanumeric designation) that, together with the street name, describes a physical location of a specific property. “Even numbered address” means a house number ending with the number 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, or no house number. “Odd numbered address” means a house number ending with the number 4, 3,5, 7, or 9.

- (2) “Declared Drought Response Level” means one of four levels of drought that can be declared based on the severity of drought conditions, with one being the least severe and four being the most severe.

391-3-30-.02 Applicability of Rule

These rules apply to any entity, and its customers, permitted by the Georgia Environmental Protection Division (EPD) for water withdrawal or for operation of a drinking water system.

391-3-30-.03 Outdoor Water Use Schedule During Non-Drought Periods (1) Outdoor water use other than exempted activities shall occur only as follows:

- (a) Odd-numbered addresses: outdoor water use is allowed on Tuesdays, Thursdays and Sundays.

- (b) Even-numbered addresses: outdoor water use is allowed on Mondays, Wednesdays and Saturdays.

3941-3-30-.04 Outdoor Water Use Schedule During Declared Drought Response Levels

391-3-30-.05 Exemptions (1) This rule shall not apply to the following outdoor water uses: (a) Capture and re-use of cooling system condensate or storm water in compliance with applicable local ordinances

- (b) Re-use of gray water in compliance with applicable local ordinances

- (2) The following established landscape water uses are exempt from the outdoor water use schedules of this rule.

- (a) Use of reclaimed wastewater by a designated user from a system permitted by EPD to provide reclaimed wastewater.

- (b) Irrigation of personal food gardens.

- (3) Newly (in place less than thirty days) installed landscapes are subject to the following: (a) Irrigation of newly installed landscapes is allowed any day of the week, but only during allowed hours for the drought response level in effect, for a period of 30 days following installation. - (b) For new landscapes installed by certified or licensed professionals, commercial exemptions apply.

- (4) The following golf course outdoor water uses are exempt from the outdoor water use schedules of this rule.

- (b) Irrigation of fairways during times of non-drought and Declared Drought Response Level One.

- (c) Irrigation of tees during times of non-drought and Declared Drought Response Levels One, Two and Three.

- (d) Irrigation of greens.
